description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries. These interfaces and languages provide ways of interacting with computer systems and are a common feature across many different platforms. Most systems come with some built-in command-line interface and scripting capabilities. Adversaries may use these to execute living-off-the-land binaries and scripts during post-exploitation. In containerized environments, shell spawning from a web application process is a critical indicator of code execution.

falco.trigger_condition: Spawning of shell interpreters (sh, bash, python, perl) by web application processes (e.g. flask, gunicorn, uwsgi). Falco proc.pname/proc.name chain rules that flag shell spawn from web server parent processes are the primary detection surface.

mitigation: Restrict shell access in production containers. Use seccomp profiles to block fork/exec syscalls from web application containers. Implement application-level output encoding and validation to prevent RCE via injection. Use read-only root filesystems to prevent dropper scripts from being written to disk.
